summary.text: Mike Lawler is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 17th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 after one term in the New York State Assembly. Before public office he worked as a campaign and party staffer, a county executive's adviser and a town official, and he founded a government affairs and public relations firm. He sits on the House Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees, and is running for re-election.

paragraphs.text: Mike Lawler was born in Suffern, New York, and lives in Pearl River with his wife, Doina, and their two daughters, according to his official biography.

He graduated from Manhattan College, where, according to his official biography, he earned degrees in accounting and finance and was class valedictorian; Ballotpedia lists a 2009 bachelor's degree from the college.
His office describes him as a lifelong Hudson Valley resident.
Lawler worked as a senior adviser in the office of Westchester County Executive Rob Astorino and served as executive director of the New York State Republican Party.
He founded a government affairs and public relations firm, per his official biography; Ballotpedia lists him as a partner with Checkmate Strategies.

He then served as Deputy Town Supervisor of Orangetown, New York, before running for the State Assembly, where he represented New York's 97th Assembly District from 2021 to 2022 and sat on the Aging, Banks, Education and Housing committees and as ranking member of Governmental Operations.
Lawler was elected to Congress in 2022, defeating incumbent Rep. Sean Maloney (D) 50.3% to 49.7% under different district lines, and was re-elected in 2024 with 52.1% of the vote to 45.8%.

In the House he serves on the Financial Services Committee, where he is Vice Chair of Communications, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, according to his official biography.

That biography says he introduced 58 bills in the 118th Congress, 7 of which passed the House and 1 of which became law, and that he was a leading member of the bipartisan SALT Caucus whose work contributed to the higher State and Local Tax deduction cap enacted in 2025.
He co-chairs the Moldova Caucus, Anti-Congestion Tax Caucus, Appalachian National Scenic Trail Caucus and Extreme Heat Caucus, and is a member of more than 50 other caucuses.
